subject: Clarify VAT treatment for FurniSales EU marketplace orders
messages:
From: Luca Bernardi <luca.bernardi@furnisales.it>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@furnisales.it>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 18:15:00 +0200
Subject: VAT treatment for sales via your marketplace — immediate month-end question

Hi Jordan,

Hope you’re well. We’re finalising month-end and spotted a routing question for transactions processed through Redwood’s marketplace. FurniSales is an EU-registered reseller (IT VAT ID below) and many of our buyers are business customers in Italy and Germany. Two quick asks: 

1) When we bill our customers through Redwood, should the invoice Redwood issues be net (reverse-charge) when the buyer provides a valid VAT ID, or will Redwood collect and remit VAT on those orders?

2) What proof of VAT registration do you accept? We can provide a VIES screenshot or an official certificate — we want to avoid payment holds.

We need confirmation before our June 30 run. Can you share the steps you’ll take and an estimated timeline?

FurniSales VAT: IT01234567890

Thanks,
Luca
Luca Bernardi
Head of Ops, FurniSales Srl
+39 02 1234 5678

(attachment: vat-validation-screenshot.png)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Luca Bernardi <luca.bernardi@furnisales.it>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VAT treatment for sales via your marketplace — immediate month-end question

Hi Luca — thanks for the details and the VAT ID.

Short answer: if the buyer is a VAT-registered business in the EU and supplies a valid VAT ID, we can apply the reverse-charge (net) treatment on the invoice Redwood issues. If the buyer cannot provide a valid VAT ID, standard VAT will be charged and remitted in the buyer’s jurisdiction.

What we need from you to proceed without a hold:
- A VIES validation screenshot OR an official national VAT certificate (both acceptable). You already attached a screenshot which helps — we’ll run our verification too.
- A quick confirmation from the buyer that they’re VAT-registered (if possible) — helps speed QA.

Operational steps and timeline (estimate):
1) Today (same day receipt): Finance runs VIES + local registry check (1 business day).
2) Day 1: If validated, we mark the customer as "VAT-registered" in billing and flag invoices to be net going forward.
3) Day 2–3: Apply reverse-charge treatment for any unsettled invoices in the current billing window; move any invoices on hold to processing.

CC’ing Ben from billing and Marissa from tax/legal to confirm accounting entries and any self-billing paperwork we should collect. Ben/Marissa — can you confirm the tolerance for a 24–72h turnaround and whether we require a signed self-billing statement for FurniSales vs. just the VAT evidence?

Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Luca Bernardi <luca.bernardi@furnisales.it>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VAT treatment for sales via your marketplace — immediate month-end question

On Mon, Jun 1, 2026 at 11:48 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Jordan: short answer...

Thanks Jordan — confirming from Finance. 

Checklist and clarifications for FurniSales: 
- Evidence accepted: VIES snapshot OR national certificate; if VIES returns an unknown status we ask for the national OS record (PDF).
- If FurniSales is the seller of record on the invoice Redwood issues, we will apply reverse-charge (net) provided: (a) buyer VAT ID validated, (b) buyer is a B2B business, and (c) we have the correct entity mapping in our accounting system.
- For the June billing run we can: 
  * Place current unpaid invoices into a temporary "VAT validation" hold (max 14 days) while we verify; OR
  * Proceed with net invoices immediately if we validate within 48 hours.

Attached: draft-mop-rc.xlsx (worked example) — shows how tax lines will be generated and where reverse-charge notes appear on the invoice. If you prefer, we can also push a short self-billing addendum to FurniSales to sign; it speeds month-end reconciliation but is not strictly required in all jurisdictions.

Operational owner: finance@redwood.com — please send the VIES screenshot and the buyer confirmation to that alias. We’ll reply with the specific invoice IDs we’ll adjust.

Ben Carter
Billing Lead, Redwood Inference
(attachment: draft-mop-rc.xlsx)

Attached is a higher-resolution VIES validation and the buyer acceptance note (we asked our key B2B customers to confirm their VAT status). We’re happy to sign a short self-billing addendum if that makes reconciliation easier — please send over a one-page PDF.

If you can confirm by EOD Europe time on June 3 that Redwood will apply reverse-charge on outstanding items, we’ll release payment on our end this week.
